label: 'Brad' Sorensen
narrative: Everything substantive on this thread traces to one man, and the earliest document that carries him gives him a first name only. William B. Scott, then senior engineering editor of Aviation Week and Space Technology, interviewed 'Brad' for one paid hour in his Pasadena office on 3 December 1990 and compiled sixteen typed pages from two tapes. The profile there is of a mid-thirties Pasadena Art Center graduate with his own design business and clients including ski and motorcycle manufacturers, who claims a private pilot's licence but, in the interviewer's own note, 'didn't seem to have a lot of knowledge about military aircraft types'. He had refused to talk the previous summer, he told Scott he wished he had never seen the craft, and he disowned part of the drawing McCandlish had made from his description. The surname Sorensen reaches the record through McCandlish, not through this document, and no opened record carries it in the witness's own voice or over his own signature.
